recognize_zh: 同一視野中三個嗜中性球的核都分成 6 葉以上（hypersegmented neutrophils），背景紅血球有淚滴狀、橢圓形等大小與形狀不一的變化並有大型血小板；在 JAK2 陽性骨髓增生性腫瘤中，須考慮 hydroxyurea 等藥物或合併葉酸/B12 缺乏。
features: Three neutrophils each with six or more nuclear lobes (hypersegmentation)
Neutrophils of normal to slightly increased size with fine pink granular cytoplasm
Marked anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop cells (dacrocytes) and elliptocytes
Large/giant platelet and a platelet clump
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows three neutrophils in a single field, each with six or more nuclear lobes, meeting criteria for neutrophil hypersegmentation. The red cells show marked anisopoikilocytosis with teardrop cells and elliptocytes, and there is a large platelet and a platelet clump. No blasts or nucleated red cells are seen in this field. In a JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasm, hypersegmentation raises the possibility of hydroxyurea (or other antimetabolite) effect or concurrent vitamin B12/folate deficiency, while the teardrop cells may reflect marrow fibrosis. Findings are consistent with hypersegmented neutrophils in a JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasm.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic anemia also shows hypersegmented neutrophils but with macro-ovalocytes, raised MCV and low B12/folate levels rather than JAK2 positivity and teardrop cells.
Drug-induced hypersegmentation occurs with macrocytosis in treated patients and is identified by medication history rather than morphology alone.
This benign autosomal dominant trait shows hypersegmentation in a proportion of neutrophils in otherwise normal blood without poikilocytosis or a clonal marker.
PMF shows leukoerythroblastosis with teardrop cells and giant platelets but does not itself cause consistent neutrophil hypersegmentation.
